commands.name: openspec-apply-change
commands.description: Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change. Use when the user wants to start implementing, continue implementation, or work through tasks. Also use when the user says "openspec apply", "opsx apply", or "openspec implement". (managed)

commands.name: deep-research
commands.description: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. (dynamic workflow)

commands.description: Grant or revoke Claude agent access to your Design projects

commands.name: design-sync
commands.description: Push a React design system to claude.ai/design. This runs a converter that bundles the real component code (from Storybook or a bare package) and uploads it. Use when the user runs /design-sync or says "sync my design system to Claude Design".

commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".

commands.name: update-config
commands.description: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.

commands.name: debug
commands.description: Enable debug logging for this session and help diagnose issues

commands.name: code-review
commands.description: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's review recipe covers them) at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.

commands.name: simplify
commands.description: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

commands.name: batch
commands.description: Research and plan a large-scale change, then execute it in parallel across 5–30 isolated worktree agents that each open a PR.

commands.name: fewer-permission-prompts
commands.description: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.

commands.name: doctor
commands.description: Health-check the user's Claude Code setup and fix issues: diagnose installation health — what the `claude doctor` terminal diagnostics cover — from local data (duplicate or leftover installs, PATH, unparseable settings files, broken or colliding agent definitions, skills whose frontmatter fails to parse); find unused skills, MCP servers, and plugins versus their context cost and disable dead weight; deduplicate local CLAUDE.md files against checked-in ones; trim checked-in CLAUDE.md files by cutting content a session could derive from the codebase (directory layouts, tech-stack lists, architecture overviews) while keeping gotchas, rationale, and non-standard conventions; migrate always-loaded CLAUDE.md guidance into lazy skills and nested CLAUDE.md files; flag slow hooks and context-heavy extensions; check the installed version is current; make auto mode the default permission mode; and pre-approve frequently denied read-only commands. Use when the user asks for a doctor run, checkup, audit, tune-up, or cleanup of their Claude Code setup or configuration.

commands.name: loop
commands.description: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace.

commands.name: schedule
commands.description: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule.

commands.name: claude-api
commands.description:
Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /etc/claude-code/.claude/skills/openspec-apply-change

Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change.

**Store selection:** If the user names a store (a store is a standalone OpenSpec repo registered on this machine) or the work lives in one, run `openspec store list --json` to discover registered store ids, then pass `--store <id>` on the commands that read or write specs and changes (`new change`, `status`, `instructions`, `list`, `show`, `validate`, `archive`, `doctor`, `context`, `schemas`, `view`). Once selected, treat `--store <id>` as sticky for the rest of the workflow. Every unscoped example of those commands below is shorthand: before running it, append the flag. For example, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json --store "<id>"`, not the unscoped form shown below. Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

**Project check:** These steps expect a project that already uses OpenSpec. Before the first step that writes anything (`new change`, `archive`, `sync specs`, or authoring an artifact file), confirm the project has a root: run `openspec list --json` (with `--store <id>` when a store is selected, since the store is then the root) and read `root`. A root object means the project is set up. `"root": null` means it is not - there is no `openspec/` directory here, and a write such as `openspec new change` would create one as a side effect. The command also exits non-zero, which is that answer rather than a broken CLI, so read the JSON instead of retrying or working around it.

One `"root": null` is not about setup: when a `status` error message starts with `Declared in` or `Invalid store declaration in` and names this project's `openspec/config.yaml` (or `config.yml`), the project does use OpenSpec through a store it declares, which this machine cannot resolve (the store is not registered, or the `store:` line is malformed). Do not treat it as uninitialized and skip the branches below: stop before writing and show the user that error's `message` and `fix`.

Otherwise, with no root, what happens next depends on how this workflow was reached:

- **Auto-selected**: you chose this workflow yourself, without the user naming OpenSpec, naming this skill, or running its slash command. Stop using OpenSpec and answer the request normally, as you would with no OpenSpec installed. Do not ask them to set anything up and do not mention OpenSpec setup.
- **Explicit OpenSpec request**: the user named OpenSpec, named this skill, or ran its slash command. Stop before writing and ask how to proceed: set this project up (`openspec init`), target a store they already have (`--store <id>`), or continue without OpenSpec for this request. Wait for their answer.

In both branches, never create the root as a side effect: do not run `openspec init` until the user asks for it, do not hand-create `openspec/` files, and do not let a command create it.

**Input**: Optionally specify a change name (e.g., `/opsx:apply add-auth`). If omitted, check if it can be inferred from conversation context. If vague or ambiguous you MUST prompt for available changes.

**Steps**

1. **Select the change**

   If a name is provided, use it. Otherwise:
   - Infer from conversation context if the user mentioned a change
   - Auto-select if only one active change exists
   - If ambiguous, run `openspec list --json` to get available changes and ask the user to select one

   Always announce: "Using change: <name>" and how to override (e.g., `/opsx:apply <other>`).

2. **Check status to understand the schema**
   ```bash
   openspec status --change "<name>" --json
   ```
   Parse the JSON to understand:
   - `schemaName`: The workflow being used (e.g., "spec-driven")
   - `planningHome`, `changeRoot`, and `actionContext`: planning scope and edit constraints
   - Which artifact contains the tasks (typically "tasks" for spec-driven, check status for others)

3. **Get apply instructions**

   ```bash
   openspec instructions apply --change "<name>" --json
   ```

   This returns:
   - `contextFiles`: artifact ID -> array of concrete file paths (varies by schema - could be proposal/specs/design/tasks or spec/tests/implementation/docs)
   - Progress (total, complete, remaining)
   - Task list with status, source path, and source line
   - Dynamic instruction based on current state
   - Optional `context`: current required project instruction input from the selected root
   - Optional `operationGuidance`: current advisory guidance for apply
   - `missingArtifacts` (when present): required artifact ids with no output

   **Handle states:**
   - If `state: "blocked"`: show the message and pause implementation.
     - If `missingArtifacts` is non-empty: suggest completing the missing artifacts. Run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`, select the next `ready` artifact (not `skipped` or `blocked`), and use `openspec instructions "<artifact-id>" --change "<name>" --json` for its rules and template. Keep the selected `--store <id>` on both commands.
     - Otherwise, follow the CLI instruction to create or repair the schema-configured tracking file from existing planning artifacts. Do not assume another artifact is ready or start implementation while blocked.
   - If `state: "all_done"`: report that all tracked tasks are complete and suggest review or verification as appropriate before archiving
   - Otherwise: proceed to implementation

   Treat `context` as a required prompt-level input. Read and consider it, and
   apply relevant project facts, conventions, and constraints while implementing.
   Treat `operationGuidance` as optional additive advice. Read and consider every
   entry, and follow entries that are applicable and compatible with the built-in
   workflow.

   Keep both fields separate from CLI-returned state, missing artifacts, tasks,
   progress, `contextFiles`, and the built-in `instruction`. They are not
   evidence of task completion, do not replace the built-in instruction, and do
   not permit bypassing a blocked state. If context conflicts with the built-in
   instruction, an explicit user choice, or a CLI-controlled value, report the
   conflict and preserve the controlling value. If guidance is inapplicable or
   conflicts with those controlling inputs, do not follow it and explain why.
   These are prompt-level behavior contracts, not enforceable checks.

4. **Read context files**

   Read every file path listed under `contextFiles` from the apply instructions output.
   The files depend on the schema being used:
   - **spec-driven**: proposal, specs, design, tasks
   - Other schemas: follow the contextFiles from CLI output

   Do not copy `context` or `operationGuidance` verbatim into implementation
   files or planning artifacts unless the user separately asks for that content.

5. **Show current progress**

   Display:
   - Schema being used
   - Progress: "N/M tasks complete"
   - Remaining tasks overview
   - Dynamic instruction from CLI

6. **Implement tasks (loop until done or blocked)**

   For each pending task:
   - Show which task is being worked on
   - Make the code changes required
   - Keep changes minimal and focused
   - Before editing, confirm the checkbox at the returned `sourcePath` and `line` still matches the task description; if it does not, rerun the apply instructions and use the refreshed location
   - Mark the task complete at its returned `sourcePath` and `line`: `- [ ]` → `- [x]`
   - Rerun the apply instructions and confirm that task is now done and progress changed
   - Continue to next task

   **Pause if:**
   - Task is unclear → ask for clarification
   - Implementation reveals a design issue → suggest updating artifacts
   - A task needs work beyond what the spec and tasks describe, or you are tempted to drop, narrow, defer, or accept exceptions to specified behavior to make it fit → surface the added scope and ask; do not absorb it silently
   - Error or blocker encountered → report and wait for guidance
   - User interrupts

7. **On completion or pause, show status**

   Display:
   - Tasks completed this session
   - Overall progress: "N/M tasks complete"
   - If all done: report that tracked tasks are complete and suggest review or verification as appropriate before archiving
   - If paused: explain why and wait for guidance

**Output During Implementation**

```
## Implementing: <change-name> (schema: <schema-name>)

Working on task 3/7: <task description>
[...implementation happening...]
✓ Task complete

Working on task 4/7: <task description>
[...implementation happening...]
✓ Task complete
```

**Output On Completion**

```
## Implementation Complete

**Change:** <change-name>
**Schema:** <schema-name>
**Progress:** 7/7 tasks complete ✓

### Completed This Session
- [x] Task 1
- [x] Task 2
...

All tracked tasks are complete. Review or verify the change as appropriate
before archiving. You can archive this change with `/opsx:archive`.
```

**Output On Pause (Issue Encountered)**

```
## Implementation Paused

**Change:** <change-name>
**Schema:** <schema-name>
**Progress:** 4/7 tasks complete

### Issue Encountered
<description of the issue>

**Options:**
1. <option 1>
2. <option 2>
3. Other approach

What would you like to do?
```

**Guardrails**
- Keep going through tasks until done or blocked
- Always read context files before starting (from the apply instructions output)
- If task is ambiguous, pause and ask before implementing
- If implementation reveals issues, pause and suggest artifact updates
- Keep code changes minimal and scoped to each task
- Update task checkbox immediately after completing each task
- Pause on errors, blockers, or unclear requirements - don't guess
- When a task needs work beyond what the spec describes, surface the added scope and pause - never silently narrow, defer, or simplify away specified behavior
- Only mark a task `- [x]` when its specified behavior is fully implemented, not when it is partially done or deferred
- Use contextFiles from CLI output, don't assume specific file names
- Use each task's sourcePath and line to update its exact checkbox
- Do not use context or operation guidance as proof that a task is complete
- Apply relevant project context; report conflicts with controlling workflow inputs
- Consider every guidance entry; explain any inapplicable or conflicting advice
- Do not copy runtime context or operation guidance into implementation files or planning artifacts
- Preserve CLI-controlled blocked/ready/all-done behavior and completion criteria

**Fluid Workflow Integration**

This skill supports the "actions on a change" model:

- **Can be invoked anytime**: Before all artifacts are done (if tasks exist), after partial implementation, interleaved with other actions
- **Allows artifact updates**: If implementation reveals design issues, suggest updating artifacts - not phase-locked, work fluidly

1	# Decisions: pc-301
2	
3	Ticket: PC-301 Record a pet's microchip number
4	
5	## Decided
6	
7	- **D1** The term is **microchip number**. "Chip number", "chip ID" and "transponder" are not used. Asked as Q1, answered 2026-10-31.
8	- **D2** The microchip number is optional on both the add form and the edit form. Asked as Q2, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: required on both forms.
9	- **D3** A microchip number must be exactly 15 digits: ISO 11784 only. Asked as Q3, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: also accepting 9- or 10-character non-ISO chips (AVID, FDX-A).
10	- **D4** A microchip number is unique across all pets of all owners, not only within one owner. Asked as Q4, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: unique per owner.
11	- **D5** PC-301 only records the microchip number. Looking up a pet by its microchip number is a separate ticket. Asked as Q5, answered 2026-10-31.
12	- **D6** The owner's page shows each pet's microchip number with the pet's other details. Asked as Q6, answered 2026-10-31.
13	- **D7** The edit form accepts a new microchip number for a pet that already has one, under the same rules as adding. Asked as Q7, answered 2026-10-31.
14	- **D8** An empty microchip number on the edit form removes the stored number. The edit form must show the stored number, so clearing it is deliberate. Asked as Q8, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: an empty field keeps the old number.

- **F3** Pet names are unique per owner, enforced by the controller (`PetController.java:110-112`, `141-144`) and by the constraint `unique_owner_pet_name` (`db/h2/schema.sql:55`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:45`), which the controller recognises by name (`PetController.java:193-196`).
- **F4** On MySQL the owner-and-name unique constraint has no name (`db/mysql/schema.sql:47`), so the name check in F3 probably doesn't match there. INFERRED, not tested.
- **F5** No pet search exists. `OwnerRepository` only finds owners.
- **F6** Controllers must leave field validation to the form's Validator (`ArchitectureTests.java:36-41`). `PetValidator` has no repository access.
- **F7** The owner's page shows each pet's name, birth date and type. Source: `src/main/resources/templates/owners/ownerDetails.html:52-56`.
- **F8** None of the 13 seeded pets has a microchip number. Source: `src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql`.
- **F9** The messages "is required" and "is already in use" already exist (`src/main/resources/messages/messages.properties:2,4`). `I18nPropertiesSyncTest` exists, so a new message probably has to be added to every locale's message file (INFERRED).
- **F10** A duplicate pet name caught by the database is shown on the form (`PetController.java:121-128`, `152-159`).
- **F11** One added `result.rejectValue("microchipNumber", "duplicate", …)` in `processCreationForm` fails `ArchitectureTests` ("was violated (1 times)"). The freeze store ignores line numbers but counts calls per method. Source: the harness probe reported in the reviews of 31 October (Opus R1, Sonnet R1); not re-run for this log.
- **F12** The H2 and MySQL seed scripts insert pets by position, with five values (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`, e.g. `INSERT IGNORE INTO pets VALUES (1, 'Leo', '2000-09-07', 1, 1);`). The Postgres one names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36-48`). MySQL and Postgres run `schema.sql` and `data.sql` at every start (`spring.sql.init.mode=always`, `application-mysql.properties:7`, `application-postgres.properties:7`). Source: review of round 3 (R1), checked again for this log. That MySQL then fails to start on a six-column table is INFERRED, not run.
- **F13** `PostgresIntegrationTests` starts Postgres through Spring Boot's Docker Compose support (`PostgresIntegrationTests.java:51-52`) and skips itself without Docker (`PostgresIntegrationTests.java:68`). `MySqlIntegrationTests` uses a Testcontainers container with `@ServiceConnection` and `@Testcontainers(disabledWithoutDocker = true)` (`MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43-49`). `pom.xml:162-186` has `spring-boot-testcontainers`, `spring-boot-docker-compose`, `testcontainers-junit-jupiter` and `testcontainers-mysql`, and no `testcontainers-postgresql`.

## Open

- None on PC-301's frontier. Two follow-ups are outside this change: looking up a pet by its microchip number (D5), and the unnamed MySQL pet-name constraint (D13, F4). Both need their own tickets. The lookup ticket also fixes the wrong-pet case accepted in D22, and has the microchip number on the visit form on its list (D24).

## 0. Release 1: column lists for the seed inserts

- [x] 0.1 Give the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` a column list (`id, name, birth_date, type_id, owner_id`), because they insert by position today (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`). Change nothing else: no schema change, no migration script, no microchip number. Leave `db/postgres/data.sql` unchanged: it already names its columns. Verify: the app starts on H2, `./mvnw test` passes with no failures beyond those noted at the baseline, and the release-1 diff touches only those two files. Where Docker is available, also run `MySqlIntegrationTests`; without Docker it is skipped, so report it as not run.
- [ ] 0.2 The two releases are two pull requests, in order (D28, design Decision 8). PR 1 is task 0.1 alone: the column lists in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql`. PR 2 is the rest of the change. The order: merge PR 1; deploy it, with no instance of the code before it left running; run the migration script; merge PR 2; deploy it. Rollback from release 2 redeploys release 1. The coding agent does not commit: both pull requests are cut from the settled working tree by path, so no task of release 2 touches those two files. Verify: no change outside task 0.1 touches `db/h2/data.sql` or `db/mysql/data.sql`.

## Release 2: the microchip number

13	- **Open session.** `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (`application.properties:11`). VERIFIED.
14	- **Message files.** `I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync` requires every key of `messages.properties` in every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en` (`I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java:112-127`). VERIFIED.
15	
16	## Goals / Non-Goals
17	
18	**Goals:**
19	
20	- Put the format and uniqueness rules in `PetValidator`, so the add and edit forms share them and the architecture rule's intent holds.
21	- Make the database the final guard against duplicates, under one constraint name on all three databases.
22	
23	**Non-Goals:**
24	
25	- No index or query for finding a pet by its microchip number beyond what the uniqueness check needs (D5).
26	- No change to the owner-and-pet-name constraint on MySQL (D13).
27	- No schema migration tool. The project has none, so the migration scripts of Decision 8 are applied by hand (known gap, D23).
28	- No microchip number on the visit form (D24). It goes on the list for the lookup ticket (D5).
29	
30	## Decisions
31	
32	### 1. Storage: a nullable `microchip_number` column, with no number stored as NULL
33	
34	`pets.microchip_number` is `VARCHAR(15)` on H2 and MySQL and `TEXT` on Postgres, matching each script's existing style. It is nullable. "No microchip number" is stored as `NULL`, never as `''`. A unique constraint allows any number of NULLs on H2, MySQL and Postgres, but only one `''` (INFERRED from each database's documented behaviour). An empty string would therefore make the second pet without a number a duplicate (see the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number").
35	
36	*Alternative rejected:* `CHAR(15)`. It pads values, and the format check already fixes the length.
37	
38	### 2. Normalisation in `Pet.setMicrochipNumber`
39	
40	The setter trims the value and removes every `' '`. If the result is empty, it stores `null`. Other characters, including dashes, dots and inner tabs, are left in place for the validator to reject (D9). Putting this in the entity means that whatever path sets the value, the validator, the uniqueness query and the stored column all see the same normalised string.
41	
42	*Alternative rejected:* a `PropertyEditor` registered in `PetController.initPetBinder`. It works only for web binding, and validator tests would have to repeat the normalisation.
43	
44	### 3. Format check: `[0-9]{15}` in `PetValidator`
45	
46	The check uses `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, so that the rule cannot quietly widen to other digit characters if the pattern ever gets Unicode flags. The error code is `microchipNumber.invalid`, following the existing `telephone.invalid` (`messages.properties:34`), with the message "must be 15 digits". The prefix (country or manufacturer code) is not checked (D15).
47	
48	### 4. Uniqueness check in `PetValidator`, through two exists queries on `OwnerRepository`
49	
50	Per D27 (G9), which reverses this decision's earlier choice of a new `PetRepository`. The pet stays behind its owner (baseline A1): there is no `PetRepository`. `OwnerRepository` gets two JPQL `@Query` methods that join through the owner's pets (`FROM Owner owner JOIN owner.pets pet`) and test the number and the id on the same joined pet:
51	
52	- `existsPetWithMicrochipNumber(String)`, for a new pet, and
53	- `existsAnotherPetWithMicrochipNumber(String, Integer)`, for an existing pet (D14): `pet.microchipNumber = :microchipNumber AND pet.id <> :petId`.
54	
55	Both select a count as a boolean, so they load no owner. Two methods are needed because `id <> NULL` is never true in SQL. A single "another pet" query called with a null id would never find a duplicate on the add form. `PetValidator` gets a constructor that takes `OwnerRepository`, and `PetController` builds it from the `OwnerRepository` it already has: its constructor is unchanged. The uniqueness query runs only when the format check passes (D17), so the field gets at most one error. The error code is the existing `duplicate` ("is already in use", `messages.properties:4`), and the error carries no argument that names the other pet (D11).
56	
57	Because the controller's constructor is unchanged, `PetControllerCharacterizationTests` needs no new mock: the approved edit that added one (T4) is reverted, and the file is as it was at `week-3-start` (D27).
58	
59	On edit, the bound `pet` is a detached entity (`open-in-view=false`), so the `exists` query cannot flush the half-edited pet first. INFERRED, and covered by the G3 test (D21, task 3.5), which runs on H2. Task 3 otherwise runs on mocked repositories and cannot show this.
60	
61	*Alternatives rejected:*
62	
63	- A check in the controller, as the pet-name check does today. It adds a `rejectValue` call that the frozen rule exists to stop.
64	- A new `PetRepository`, as this decision first chose. It departs from baseline A1, which keeps a pet behind its owner, and G9 kept the check behind `OwnerRepository` instead (D27). The reason first given against `OwnerRepository`, that a pet-level exists query does not belong there and that loading every owner to scan their pets would not scale, does not hold: A1 says the query belongs there, and an exists query loads no owner.
65	- A derived query such as `existsByPetsMicrochipNumberAndPetsIdNot`. Whether Spring Data tests both properties on the same join is not stated in the method name; the JPQL makes it explicit, and task 1.3 tests it.
66	
67	### 5. Database duplicates are rejected by a `PetValidator` method that the controller's `catch` calls
68	
69	The constraint is named `unique_pet_microchip_number` on all three databases:
70	
71	- H2: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE`.
72	- MySQL: a named `CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE` inside `CREATE TABLE`.
73	- Postgres: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
74	
75	Neither constraint name is a substring of the other. Both POST handlers' `catch (DataIntegrityViolationException)` blocks check for the microchip constraint first, then the name constraint, then rethrow (spec: "Duplicate microchip numbers caught by the database", and the MODIFIED "Duplicate names caught by the database").
76	
77	The save fails after validation has run, so the validator's normal checks cannot see this case. Per D19, `PetValidator` gets a public method, for example `rejectDuplicateMicrochipNumber(Errors)`, that calls `rejectValue("microchipNumber", "duplicate")` with no argument naming another pet (D11). When the exception names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case, the controller's `catch` calls this method and shows the form again. `PetController` builds one `PetValidator` from its `OwnerRepository` (D27). It uses that validator both in `initPetBinder` and in the two `catch` blocks.
78	
79	Both matchers, `isDuplicateMicrochipNumberViolation` and the existing `isDuplicatePetNameViolation`, lower-case the message with `Locale.ROOT`, so that the match does not depend on the server's default locale: in Turkish, for example, `"I".toLowerCase()` is a dotless `ı`, and `UNIQUE_PET_MICROCHIP_NUMBER` would not match (D29). Fixing the name matcher is beyond PC-301; D29 records it.
80	
81	No new `rejectValue` call is added to `PetController`. The four frozen calls of the name mapping (F10) stay as they are, and so does the freeze store. The implementer must not regenerate or edit the freeze store. If `ArchitectureTests` fails anyway, they stop and raise it with the ticket owner (task 4.3).
82	
83	*Alternatives rejected:*
84	
85	- One `rejectValue` call per `catch` that chooses the field from the error, `name` or `microchipNumber`. It reshapes the name mapping that the characterisation tests pin (D19).
86	- A waiver for two more frozen violations. It weakens the sensor (D19).
87	- `@ControllerAdvice`. It avoids the rule instead of meeting it (D19).
88	- New `rejectValue` calls in the controller, next to the name mapping. The probe shows that the freeze store rejects them (F11).
89	- Run the validator again after the failed save, so that the `exists` query finds the winning row. It depends on the other transaction's commit being visible and on the failed persistence context not flushing again. That is too fragile for a race-condition path.
90	
91	### 6. The edit copy includes the microchip number
92	
93	`updatePetDetails` also copies `microchipNumber`, including `null`, so that clearing the field removes the number (D8).
94	
95	### 7. Views and messages
96	
97	- Two new keys:
98	  - `microchipNumber=Microchip number` (glossary term, D1)
99	  - `microchipNumber.invalid=must be 15 digits`
100	
101	  Both go in `messages.properties` and every locale file except `messages_en`.
102	- `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` gets a text input for `microchipNumber` through the existing `inputField` fragment, after the birth date. `th:field` fills it with the stored value on edit (spec: "The edit form shows the stored microchip number").
103	- `owners/ownerDetails.html` gets `<dt th:text="#{microchipNumber}">` and `<dd th:text="${pet.microchipNumber}">` after the type (`ownerDetails.html:55-56`). A `null` renders as an empty `dd` (INFERRED Thymeleaf behaviour), which is what D16 asks for.
104	
105	### 8. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are migrated by one script each
106	
107	Per D23, which replaces D20, as amended by D25. On an existing database, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets` is skipped (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`, VERIFIED), so the new column would never be created there. `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`, `application-postgres.properties:7`, VERIFIED) runs `schema.sql` on every start, so release 2 would meet a table without the column (review R1; the exact failure is INFERRED, not run).
108	
109	The scripts:
110	
111	- `db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN microchip_number VARCHAR(15) NULL`, then `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT unique_pet_microchip_number UNIQUE (microchip_number)`.
112	- `db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS microchip_number TEXT`, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number ON pets (microchip_number)`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
113	- None for H2: it is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
114	
115	Column types and the constraint name match Decisions 1 and 5. The scripts sit under `src/main/resources/db/<database>/` but are not run at start: `spring.sql.init` reads only `schema.sql` and `data.sql` there (`application.properties:3-4`, VERIFIED). The `schema.sql` files still create the column and the constraint for new databases (task 1.1). Each script starts with a comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25).
116	
117	The change ships in two releases (D25, which amends D23). D23 said the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column. On MySQL that is false: the old `db/mysql/data.sql` inserts pets by position with five values (`db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`, VERIFIED) and runs at every start (`application-mysql.properties:7`, VERIFIED), so the old code cannot start against a six-column table (review R1; the exact MySQL error is INFERRED, not run). It holds from release 1 on, because release 1 names the columns.
118	
119	Per D28 (G10), which amends D25, the two releases are two pull requests. A pull request is what deploys: two commits in one pull request would deploy together and lose the order. The pull requests are cut from the settled working tree by path, so no work for release 2 touches the two files of release 1.
120	
121	- **Release 1** is PR 1. It ships only the column lists for the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` (task 0.1). Nothing else changes. With a column list, the inserts work on the old table and on the migrated one, where the nullable `microchip_number` is left `NULL` (INFERRED, not run). The Postgres `data.sql` already names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36-48`, VERIFIED), so release 1 changes nothing for Postgres.
122	- **Release 2** is PR 2. It ships the microchip number: everything else in this change, including the migration scripts (tasks 1.1 to 5.1).
123	
124	Deployment, in order:
125	
126	1. Merge PR 1.
127	2. Deploy release 1, and make sure no instance of the code before it is still running or can be restarted.
128	3. Run the script for the database against the existing database, while release 1 is still running. Release 1 keeps working against the new table, because its seed inserts name their columns and the rest of it never names the new column (D25).
129	4. Merge PR 2.
130	5. Deploy release 2. Its `schema.sql` skips `CREATE TABLE`, and on Postgres the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number` finds the index the script made (INFERRED; task 1.5 checks it).
131	
132	Rollback from release 2, in order:
133	
134	1. Redeploy release 1. It works on the migrated table (D25). Do not redeploy the code before release 1: on MySQL it cannot start against the migrated table.
135	2. Leave the column and the constraint in place. Dropping them is a separate, later step, not part of this change.
136	
137	The change stays one OpenSpec change; the two releases are two pull requests, merged and deployed in the order above (D28, amending D25).
138	
139	*Alternative rejected:* a migration tool such as Flyway or Liquibase. A real team would use one, but PetClinic has none (known gap, D23).
140	
141	### 9. Each scenario declares its level, and tests are named after the scenarios they show
142	
143	Per D30 (G12), each scenario of the spec deltas ends with `- **CHECKED AT** <level>`: the lowest level at which its outcome can be observed, from `unit` < `form` < `database` < `mysql-postgres` < `concurrency` < `manual`. PC-301 has 11 `unit`, 14 `form`, 5 `database` and 2 `concurrency` scenarios (task 7.1).
144	
145	Per D31 (G13), a test shows a scenario by its name alone: the scenario's title in lowerCamelCase, with punctuation and apostrophes dropped, and possibly more words after it (for example `theConstraintIsReportedAsADuplicateNameOnTheEditForm`). The test's level comes from its class: `@WebMvcTest` is `form`; `@SpringBootTest` is `database`, and `form` as well when it drives MockMvc or HTTP; threads against a running app are `concurrency`; a class with no Spring test annotation is `unit`. Existing tests are renamed to this rule, with no body change (task 7.2). This lets step 5's scenario-coverage sensor check, by name and level, that each scenario has a test.
146	
147	## Risks / Trade-offs
148	
149	- [Existing MySQL or Postgres databases keep their old `pets` table, because `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skips it] → The migration scripts of Decision 8 add the column and the constraint after release 1 and before release 2 is deployed (D23, D25). H2 is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
150	- [Release 2 is deployed before the migration script has run] → The steps in Decision 8 put the script before release 2. Nothing in the app enforces the order, because PetClinic has no migration tool (known gap, D23).
151	- [The H2 and MySQL seed inserts give values by position (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`), so they would not match a sixth column, and on MySQL the code before release 1 cannot start against the migrated table (F12)] → Release 1 gives them a column list before the script runs (task 0.1, D25). Rollback goes to release 1, never to the code before it. No seeded pet gets a number (F8).
152	- [Each database words its duplicate-key message differently, and H2 may put the name in upper case inside a generated index name] → The match ignores case and looks for the constraint name as a substring. Task 1.4 checks the real message on H2: it saves two pets with the same number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so the validator does not run, and asserts that the `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. The race test (task 4.2) does not check the real message. If one request commits before the other's `exists` query runs, the validator rejects the loser and the `catch` never runs, and the page looks the same either way. The `catch` itself is covered with mocked messages (task 4.1).
153	- **Known gap** (recorded with D20; D23 does not change it): the duplicate is not tested through the forms on MySQL or Postgres. Their integration tests run only with Docker (`MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43`, `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:67-68`), and they do not exercise the microchip constraint. This is left as it is.
154	- **Known gaps** (D23): PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand and nothing records whether a database has been migrated. The migration tests (task 1.5) run only with Docker; without it they are skipped, and must be reported as not run rather than as passed. They add no dependency: they follow the existing `MySqlIntegrationTests` and `PostgresIntegrationTests` (D26, F13).
155	- [A pet with no owner (`owner_id` null, as the PC-302 defect can leave behind) is not found by the exists queries, because they join through owners (D27)] → The validator lets such a number through, but the database constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` still rejects it, and the `catch` reports it as "is already in use" on the microchip number (Decision 5). PC-302 is its own ticket.
156	- [The validator now issues one query per submission that has a microchip number] → It is an indexed `exists` query on the unique constraint, so the cost is negligible.
157	- [Translations into nine languages may be poor] → The sync test checks only that the keys are present. Translations should be reviewed by a speaker before release, as for any new label.
158	- [A microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it] → Accepted until the lookup ticket (D22, following from D5 and D11).

# Design

## Context

See `proposal.md` for the motivation, and `specs/pets/spec.md` and `specs/owner-details/spec.md` for the requirements. The facts below shape how the change is built. Each is labelled VERIFIED (code opened) or INFERRED (not checked).

- **Validation placement.** `ArchitectureTests.java:36-43` forbids controllers from calling `Errors.rejectValue`, because field validation belongs in `PetValidator`. The rule is wrapped in `freeze(...)`, so the calls that already exist are recorded in `src/test/resources/archunit_store/1cbfc1d1-…` and tolerated. That includes the four calls in `PetController`'s two POST handlers. VERIFIED. The store counts calls per method, so one more `rejectValue` call in a POST handler fails the rule (F11, from the reviewers' probe; not re-run here).
- **Validator wiring.** `PetValidator` is created with `new PetValidator()` in `PetController.initPetBinder` (`PetController.java:95`). It has no repository (F6). VERIFIED.
- **Pet ids.** The `id` field cannot be bound from the form (`PetController.java:96`). On edit, the `pet` model attribute is the owner's pet loaded by the path's `petId` (`PetController.java:74-86`). So `pet.getId()` can be trusted when excluding a pet's own number. VERIFIED.
- **Edit copies fields.** `updatePetDetails` copies name, birth date and type onto the owner's pet (`PetController.java:177-191`). A new field is not copied unless it is added there. VERIFIED.
- **Database violations.** `isDuplicatePetNameViolation` matches the constraint name in the exception message, ignoring case (`PetController.java:193-196`). VERIFIED.
- **Schema setup.** The schema is created by `spring.sql.init` from `db/${database}/schema.sql`, and Hibernate does not manage the DDL (`application.properties:3,10`). The MySQL and Postgres scripts use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`). VERIFIED.
- **Open session.** `spring.jpa.open-in-view=false` (`application.properties:11`). VERIFIED.
- **Message files.** `I18nPropertiesSyncTest.checkI18nPropertyFilesAreInSync` requires every key of `messages.properties` in every `messages_*.properties` except `messages_en` (`I18nPropertiesSyncTest.java:112-127`). VERIFIED.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**

- Put the format and uniqueness rules in `PetValidator`, so the add and edit forms share them and the architecture rule's intent holds.
- Make the database the final guard against duplicates, under one constraint name on all three databases.

**Non-Goals:**

- No index or query for finding a pet by its microchip number beyond what the uniqueness check needs (D5).
- No change to the owner-and-pet-name constraint on MySQL (D13).
- No schema migration tool. The project has none, so the migration scripts of Decision 8 are applied by hand (known gap, D23).
- No microchip number on the visit form (D24). It goes on the list for the lookup ticket (D5).

## Decisions

### 1. Storage: a nullable `microchip_number` column, with no number stored as NULL

`pets.microchip_number` is `VARCHAR(15)` on H2 and MySQL and `TEXT` on Postgres, matching each script's existing style. It is nullable. "No microchip number" is stored as `NULL`, never as `''`. A unique constraint allows any number of NULLs on H2, MySQL and Postgres, but only one `''` (INFERRED from each database's documented behaviour). An empty string would therefore make the second pet without a number a duplicate (see the scenario "Two pets without a microchip number").

*Alternative rejected:* `CHAR(15)`. It pads values, and the format check already fixes the length.

### 2. Normalisation in `Pet.setMicrochipNumber`

The setter trims the value and removes every `' '`. If the result is empty, it stores `null`. Other characters, including dashes, dots and inner tabs, are left in place for the validator to reject (D9). Putting this in the entity means that whatever path sets the value, the validator, the uniqueness query and the stored column all see the same normalised string.

*Alternative rejected:* a `PropertyEditor` registered in `PetController.initPetBinder`. It works only for web binding, and validator tests would have to repeat the normalisation.

### 3. Format check: `[0-9]{15}` in `PetValidator`

The check uses `[0-9]` rather than `\d`, so that the rule cannot quietly widen to other digit characters if the pattern ever gets Unicode flags. The error code is `microchipNumber.invalid`, following the existing `telephone.invalid` (`messages.properties:34`), with the message "must be 15 digits". The prefix (country or manufacturer code) is not checked (D15).

### 4. Uniqueness check in `PetValidator`, through two exists queries on `OwnerRepository`

Per D27 (G9), which reverses this decision's earlier choice of a new `PetRepository`. The pet stays behind its owner (baseline A1): there is no `PetRepository`. `OwnerRepository` gets two JPQL `@Query` methods that join through the owner's pets (`FROM Owner owner JOIN owner.pets pet`) and test the number and the id on the same joined pet:

- `existsPetWithMicrochipNumber(String)`, for a new pet, and
- `existsAnotherPetWithMicrochipNumber(String, Integer)`, for an existing pet (D14): `pet.microchipNumber = :microchipNumber AND pet.id <> :petId`.

Both select a count as a boolean, so they load no owner. Two methods are needed because `id <> NULL` is never true in SQL. A single "another pet" query called with a null id would never find a duplicate on the add form. `PetValidator` gets a constructor that takes `OwnerRepository`, and `PetController` builds it from the `OwnerRepository` it already has: its constructor is unchanged. The uniqueness query runs only when the format check passes (D17), so the field gets at most one error. The error code is the existing `duplicate` ("is already in use", `messages.properties:4`), and the error carries no argument that names the other pet (D11).

Because the controller's constructor is unchanged, `PetControllerCharacterizationTests` needs no new mock: the approved edit that added one (T4) is reverted, and the file is as it was at `week-3-start` (D27).

On edit, the bound `pet` is a detached entity (`open-in-view=false`), so the `exists` query cannot flush the half-edited pet first. INFERRED, and covered by the G3 test (D21, task 3.5), which runs on H2. Task 3 otherwise runs on mocked repositories and cannot show this.

*Alternatives rejected:*

- A check in the controller, as the pet-name check does today. It adds a `rejectValue` call that the frozen rule exists to stop.
- A new `PetRepository`, as this decision first chose. It departs from baseline A1, which keeps a pet behind its owner, and G9 kept the check behind `OwnerRepository` instead (D27). The reason first given against `OwnerRepository`, that a pet-level exists query does not belong there and that loading every owner to scan their pets would not scale, does not hold: A1 says the query belongs there, and an exists query loads no owner.
- A derived query such as `existsByPetsMicrochipNumberAndPetsIdNot`. Whether Spring Data tests both properties on the same join is not stated in the method name; the JPQL makes it explicit, and task 1.3 tests it.

### 5. Database duplicates are rejected by a `PetValidator` method that the controller's `catch` calls

The constraint is named `unique_pet_microchip_number` on all three databases:

- H2: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE`.
- MySQL: a named `CONSTRAINT … UNIQUE` inside `CREATE TABLE`.
- Postgres: `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).

Neither constraint name is a substring of the other. Both POST handlers' `catch (DataIntegrityViolationException)` blocks check for the microchip constraint first, then the name constraint, then rethrow (spec: "Duplicate microchip numbers caught by the database", and the MODIFIED "Duplicate names caught by the database").

The save fails after validation has run, so the validator's normal checks cannot see this case. Per D19, `PetValidator` gets a public method, for example `rejectDuplicateMicrochipNumber(Errors)`, that calls `rejectValue("microchipNumber", "duplicate")` with no argument naming another pet (D11). When the exception names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case, the controller's `catch` calls this method and shows the form again. `PetController` builds one `PetValidator` from its `OwnerRepository` (D27). It uses that validator both in `initPetBinder` and in the two `catch` blocks.

Both matchers, `isDuplicateMicrochipNumberViolation` and the existing `isDuplicatePetNameViolation`, lower-case the message with `Locale.ROOT`, so that the match does not depend on the server's default locale: in Turkish, for example, `"I".toLowerCase()` is a dotless `ı`, and `UNIQUE_PET_MICROCHIP_NUMBER` would not match (D29). Fixing the name matcher is beyond PC-301; D29 records it.

No new `rejectValue` call is added to `PetController`. The four frozen calls of the name mapping (F10) stay as they are, and so does the freeze store. The implementer must not regenerate or edit the freeze store. If `ArchitectureTests` fails anyway, they stop and raise it with the ticket owner (task 4.3).

*Alternatives rejected:*

- One `rejectValue` call per `catch` that chooses the field from the error, `name` or `microchipNumber`. It reshapes the name mapping that the characterisation tests pin (D19).
- A waiver for two more frozen violations. It weakens the sensor (D19).
- `@ControllerAdvice`. It avoids the rule instead of meeting it (D19).
- New `rejectValue` calls in the controller, next to the name mapping. The probe shows that the freeze store rejects them (F11).
- Run the validator again after the failed save, so that the `exists` query finds the winning row. It depends on the other transaction's commit being visible and on the failed persistence context not flushing again. That is too fragile for a race-condition path.

### 6. The edit copy includes the microchip number

`updatePetDetails` also copies `microchipNumber`, including `null`, so that clearing the field removes the number (D8).

### 7. Views and messages

- Two new keys:
  - `microchipNumber=Microchip number` (glossary term, D1)
  - `microchipNumber.invalid=must be 15 digits`

  Both go in `messages.properties` and every locale file except `messages_en`.
- `pets/createOrUpdatePetForm.html` gets a text input for `microchipNumber` through the existing `inputField` fragment, after the birth date. `th:field` fills it with the stored value on edit (spec: "The edit form shows the stored microchip number").
- `owners/ownerDetails.html` gets `<dt th:text="#{microchipNumber}">` and `<dd th:text="${pet.microchipNumber}">` after the type (`ownerDetails.html:55-56`). A `null` renders as an empty `dd` (INFERRED Thymeleaf behaviour), which is what D16 asks for.

### 8. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are migrated by one script each

Per D23, which replaces D20, as amended by D25. On an existing database, `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS pets` is skipped (`db/mysql/schema.sql:38`, `db/postgres/schema.sql:36`, VERIFIED), so the new column would never be created there. `spring.sql.init.mode=always` (`application-mysql.properties:7`, `application-postgres.properties:7`, VERIFIED) runs `schema.sql` on every start, so release 2 would meet a table without the column (review R1; the exact failure is INFERRED, not run).

The scripts:

- `db/mysql/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN microchip_number VARCHAR(15) NULL`, then `ALTER TABLE pets ADD CONSTRAINT unique_pet_microchip_number UNIQUE (microchip_number)`.
- `db/postgres/migrate-pc-301-microchip-number.sql`: `ALTER TABLE pets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS microchip_number TEXT`, then `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number ON pets (microchip_number)`, as `unique_owner_pet_name` is (`db/postgres/schema.sql:45`).
- None for H2: it is in memory and rebuilt on every start.

Column types and the constraint name match Decisions 1 and 5. The scripts sit under `src/main/resources/db/<database>/` but are not run at start: `spring.sql.init` reads only `schema.sql` and `data.sql` there (`application.properties:3-4`, VERIFIED). The `schema.sql` files still create the column and the constraint for new databases (task 1.1). Each script starts with a comment that says to run it after release 1 is deployed and before release 2 is (D25).

The change ships in two releases (D25, which amends D23). D23 said the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column. On MySQL that is false: the old `db/mysql/data.sql` inserts pets by position with five values (`db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`, VERIFIED) and runs at every start (`application-mysql.properties:7`, VERIFIED), so the old code cannot start against a six-column table (review R1; the exact MySQL error is INFERRED, not run). It holds from release 1 on, because release 1 names the columns.

Per D28 (G10), which amends D25, the two releases are two pull requests. A pull request is what deploys: two commits in one pull request would deploy together and lose the order. The pull requests are cut from the settled working tree by path, so no work for release 2 touches the two files of release 1.

- **Release 1** is PR 1. It ships only the column lists for the pet inserts in `db/h2/data.sql` and `db/mysql/data.sql` (task 0.1). Nothing else changes. With a column list, the inserts work on the old table and on the migrated one, where the nullable `microchip_number` is left `NULL` (INFERRED, not run). The Postgres `data.sql` already names its columns (`db/postgres/data.sql:36-48`, VERIFIED), so release 1 changes nothing for Postgres.
- **Release 2** is PR 2. It ships the microchip number: everything else in this change, including the migration scripts (tasks 1.1 to 5.1).

Deployment, in order:

1. Merge PR 1.
2. Deploy release 1, and make sure no instance of the code before it is still running or can be restarted.
3. Run the script for the database against the existing database, while release 1 is still running. Release 1 keeps working against the new table, because its seed inserts name their columns and the rest of it never names the new column (D25).
4. Merge PR 2.
5. Deploy release 2. Its `schema.sql` skips `CREATE TABLE`, and on Postgres the `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unique_pet_microchip_number` finds the index the script made (INFERRED; task 1.5 checks it).

Rollback from release 2, in order:

1. Redeploy release 1. It works on the migrated table (D25). Do not redeploy the code before release 1: on MySQL it cannot start against the migrated table.
2. Leave the column and the constraint in place. Dropping them is a separate, later step, not part of this change.

The change stays one OpenSpec change; the two releases are two pull requests, merged and deployed in the order above (D28, amending D25).

*Alternative rejected:* a migration tool such as Flyway or Liquibase. A real team would use one, but PetClinic has none (known gap, D23).

### 9. Each scenario declares its level, and tests are named after the scenarios they show

Per D30 (G12), each scenario of the spec deltas ends with `- **CHECKED AT** <level>`: the lowest level at which its outcome can be observed, from `unit` < `form` < `database` < `mysql-postgres` < `concurrency` < `manual`. PC-301 has 11 `unit`, 14 `form`, 5 `database` and 2 `concurrency` scenarios (task 7.1).

Per D31 (G13), a test shows a scenario by its name alone: the scenario's title in lowerCamelCase, with punctuation and apostrophes dropped, and possibly more words after it (for example `theConstraintIsReportedAsADuplicateNameOnTheEditForm`). The test's level comes from its class: `@WebMvcTest` is `form`; `@SpringBootTest` is `database`, and `form` as well when it drives MockMvc or HTTP; threads against a running app are `concurrency`; a class with no Spring test annotation is `unit`. Existing tests are renamed to this rule, with no body change (task 7.2). This lets step 5's scenario-coverage sensor check, by name and level, that each scenario has a test.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Existing MySQL or Postgres databases keep their old `pets` table, because `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` skips it] → The migration scripts of Decision 8 add the column and the constraint after release 1 and before release 2 is deployed (D23, D25). H2 is in memory and rebuilt on every start.
- [Release 2 is deployed before the migration script has run] → The steps in Decision 8 put the script before release 2. Nothing in the app enforces the order, because PetClinic has no migration tool (known gap, D23).
- [The H2 and MySQL seed inserts give values by position (`db/h2/data.sql:36-48`, `db/mysql/data.sql:36-48`), so they would not match a sixth column, and on MySQL the code before release 1 cannot start against the migrated table (F12)] → Release 1 gives them a column list before the script runs (task 0.1, D25). Rollback goes to release 1, never to the code before it. No seeded pet gets a number (F8).
- [Each database words its duplicate-key message differently, and H2 may put the name in upper case inside a generated index name] → The match ignores case and looks for the constraint name as a substring. Task 1.4 checks the real message on H2: it saves two pets with the same number through `OwnerRepository.saveAndFlush`, so the validator does not run, and asserts that the `DataIntegrityViolationException` names `unique_pet_microchip_number`, ignoring case. The race test (task 4.2) does not check the real message. If one request commits before the other's `exists` query runs, the validator rejects the loser and the `catch` never runs, and the page looks the same either way. The `catch` itself is covered with mocked messages (task 4.1).
- **Known gap** (recorded with D20; D23 does not change it): the duplicate is not tested through the forms on MySQL or Postgres. Their integration tests run only with Docker (`MySqlIntegrationTests.java:43`, `PostgresIntegrationTests.java:67-68`), and they do not exercise the microchip constraint. This is left as it is.
- **Known gaps** (D23): PetClinic has no migration tool, so the scripts are applied by hand and nothing records whether a database has been migrated. The migration tests (task 1.5) run only with Docker; without it they are skipped, and must be reported as not run rather than as passed. They add no dependency: they follow the existing `MySqlIntegrationTests` and `PostgresIntegrationTests` (D26, F13).
- [A pet with no owner (`owner_id` null, as the PC-302 defect can leave behind) is not found by the exists queries, because they join through owners (D27)] → The validator lets such a number through, but the database constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` still rejects it, and the `catch` reports it as "is already in use" on the microchip number (Decision 5). PC-302 is its own ticket.
- [The validator now issues one query per submission that has a microchip number] → It is an indexed `exists` query on the unique constraint, so the cost is negligible.
- [Translations into nine languages may be poor] → The sync test checks only that the keys are present. Translations should be reviewed by a speaker before release, as for any new label.
- [A microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it] → Accepted until the lookup ticket (D22, following from D5 and D11).

# Decisions: pc-301

Ticket: PC-301 Record a pet's microchip number

## Decided

- **D1** The term is **microchip number**. "Chip number", "chip ID" and "transponder" are not used. Asked as Q1, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D2** The microchip number is optional on both the add form and the edit form. Asked as Q2, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: required on both forms.
- **D3** A microchip number must be exactly 15 digits: ISO 11784 only. Asked as Q3, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: also accepting 9- or 10-character non-ISO chips (AVID, FDX-A).
- **D4** A microchip number is unique across all pets of all owners, not only within one owner. Asked as Q4, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: unique per owner.
- **D5** PC-301 only records the microchip number. Looking up a pet by its microchip number is a separate ticket. Asked as Q5, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D6** The owner's page shows each pet's microchip number with the pet's other details. Asked as Q6, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D7** The edit form accepts a new microchip number for a pet that already has one, under the same rules as adding. Asked as Q7, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D8** An empty microchip number on the edit form removes the stored number. The edit form must show the stored number, so clearing it is deliberate. Asked as Q8, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: an empty field keeps the old number.
- **D9** The entered value is trimmed and its spaces removed, then it must be exactly 15 digits. Only the digits are stored. Nothing else is removed (no dashes, no dots). Asked as Q9, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D10** A microchip number that is not 15 digits after D9 gets the error "must be 15 digits". A duplicate gets "is already in use". Both errors are on the microchip number field. Asked as Q10, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D11** The duplicate error is only "is already in use". The form must not show another owner's pet or details. Asked as Q11, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: naming the pet or owner that has the number.
- **D12** H2, MySQL and Postgres each get a named unique constraint on the microchip number. A duplicate caught by the database is reported as "is already in use" on the microchip number field. Where that code goes is a design decision, not part of this requirement. Asked as Q12, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D13** Fixing the unnamed MySQL pet-name constraint (F4) is not part of PC-301. It is a separate bug. Asked as Q13, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D14** A pet never conflicts with its own microchip number, compared after spaces are removed. Saving a pet again with the number it already has is accepted. Asked as Q14, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D15** Only the 15-digit check applies. The country or manufacturer code in the first three digits is not checked. Asked as Q15, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: checking against ISO 3166 numeric and manufacturer codes.
- **D16** On the owner's page, a pet without a microchip number shows the "Microchip number" label with an empty value. Asked as Q16, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: hiding the label; showing a word such as "none".
- **D17** A malformed microchip number gets the format error only. A well-formed duplicate gets "is already in use" only. Either one is reported together with the form's other errors. Asked as Q17, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D18** Where the uniqueness check lives in the code is a design decision for the change, not part of this requirement (see F6). Stated by the user on 2026-10-31.
- **D19** A duplicate caught by the database becomes the error on the microchip number field through a `PetValidator` method that rejects the field. The controller's `catch` calls that method. No new `rejectValue` call is added to a controller, and the freeze store stays as it is (F6, F11). Asked as G1 at the gate of 1 November, answered 2026-11-01. Rejected: one `rejectValue` call per `catch` that chooses the field (it reshapes the pinned name mapping); a waiver for two more frozen violations (it weakens the sensor); `@ControllerAdvice` (it avoids the rule instead of meeting it).
- **D20** *Replaced by D23 (G5, gate of 1 November, round 3); kept for the record.* PC-301 has no migration plan. Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are out of scope: the change covers the schema scripts the app starts from. No decision asked for a migration. Known gap recorded with this answer: the duplicate has no cross-database test. The MySQL and Postgres integration tests run only where Docker is available, and the change adds no microchip number test to them (Codex R3, left as it is). Asked as G2 at the gate of 1 November, answered 2026-11-01.
- **D21** One test on H2 adds a pet with a microchip number, edits it to another number, clears it, and reads the stored value after each step. The same test submits a rejected edit and reads that the stored value is unchanged. Asked as G3 at the gate of 1 November, answered 2026-11-01.
- **D22** Until the lookup ticket (D5), a microchip number typed onto the wrong pet blocks the right pet, and reception cannot see which pet holds it. This is accepted. It follows from D5 (no lookup) and D11 (the error names no other pet), and the lookup ticket is where it gets fixed. Asked as G4 at the gate of 1 November, answered 2026-11-01.
- **D23** *Amended by D25 (G7, gate of 1 November, round 4): on MySQL the premise "the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column" is false while the old `data.sql` inserts by position, and holds only from release 1 on; the deployment becomes release 1, then the script, then release 2; rollback redeploys release 1. The rest stands; text kept as answered.* Replaces D20: G2 was wrong and is reversed. A real clinic's database already holds data, so the change migrates existing MySQL and Postgres databases. It ships one migration script per database; H2 is in memory and needs none. The script adds the nullable `microchip_number` column, then the unique constraint `unique_pet_microchip_number` (a unique index on Postgres, as for pet names). It is run before the new code is deployed; the old code keeps working against the new table because it never names the column. The `schema.sql` files still create the column for new databases. Rollback: redeploy the old code and leave the column; dropping it is a separate, later step. The change documents these steps in order. Why G2 was wrong: the reviews found that the plan's steps were in the wrong order, and the recommendation at the gate called the plan added scope because no decision asked for it. # Decisions: pc-301

Ticket: PC-301 Record a pet's microchip number

## Decided

- **D1** The term is **microchip number**. "Chip number", "chip ID" and "transponder" are not used. Asked as Q1, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D2** The microchip number is optional on both the add form and the edit form. Asked as Q2, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: required on both forms.
- **D3** A microchip number must be exactly 15 digits: ISO 11784 only. Asked as Q3, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: also accepting 9- or 10-character non-ISO chips (AVID, FDX-A).
- **D4** A microchip number is unique across all pets of all owners, not only within one owner. Asked as Q4, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: unique per owner.
- **D5** PC-301 only records the microchip number. Looking up a pet by its microchip number is a separate ticket. Asked as Q5, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D6** The owner's page shows each pet's microchip number with the pet's other details. Asked as Q6, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D7** The edit form accepts a new microchip number for a pet that already has one, under the same rules as adding. Asked as Q7, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D8** An empty microchip number on the edit form removes the stored number. The edit form must show the stored number, so clearing it is deliberate. Asked as Q8, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: an empty field keeps the old number.
- **D9** The entered value is trimmed and its spaces removed, then it must be exactly 15 digits. Only the digits are stored. Nothing else is removed (no dashes, no dots). Asked as Q9, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D10** A microchip number that is not 15 digits after D9 gets the error "must be 15 digits". A duplicate gets "is already in use". Both errors are on the microchip number field. Asked as Q10, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D11** The duplicate error is only "is already in use". The form must not show another owner's pet or details. Asked as Q11, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: naming the pet or owner that has the number.
- **D12** H2, MySQL and Postgres each get a named unique constraint on the microchip number. A duplicate caught by the database is reported as "is already in use" on the microchip number field. Where that code goes is a design decision, not part of this requirement. Asked as Q12, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D13** Fixing the unnamed MySQL pet-name constraint (F4) is not part of PC-301. It is a separate bug. Asked as Q13, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D14** A pet never conflicts with its own microchip number, compared after spaces are removed. Saving a pet again with the number it already has is accepted. Asked as Q14, answered 2026-10-31.
- **D15** Only the 15-digit check applies. The country or manufacturer code in the first three digits is not checked. Asked as Q15, answered 2026-10-31. Rejected: checking against ISO 3166 numeric and manufacturer codes.

- **D17** A malformed microchip number gets the format error only. A well-formed duplicate gets "is already in use" only. Either one is reported together with the form's other errors. Asked as Q17, answered 2026-10-31.

Existing MySQL and Postgres databases are out of scope: the change covers the schema scripts the app starts from. No decision asked for a migration.
